arguments.decision_needed: Tenant reports the landlord's LG washing machine (there when they moved in) has a power failure and they believe it can't be repaired (their own web research, not diagnosed). They offer to buy a replacement that would remain their property and be taken with them when they leave. Do you consent? And what should happen to the existing machine (inspect/repair, remove, dispose, store), and may the tenant's machine stay connected? Any disconnection, removal or fitting would be at your cost, not the tenant's.
options: Consent to tenant's own machine, landlord's machine removed/stored at landlord's cost (recommended if repair not worthwhile)
Send our contractor to inspect/repair the existing LG first
Landlord arranges own contractor or replacement
Decline tenant's own machine
arguments.update: No contractor assigned and no spend committed. Job is routine. Please reply by 2025-07-29.

arguments.note: Tenant wants to replace landlord's LG washer with own machine (remains tenant's, not on inventory, taken at move-out). Needs landlord consent; not a repair. Fault undiagnosed (tenant's online research). Landlord asked re existing machine disposal/storage at landlord cost and whether tenant's may stay connected. Awaiting landlord, review 2025-07-29.

arguments.body: Hello, thanks for letting us know about the washing machine. Because the machine belongs to the landlord, and you'd like to bring in your own, we need the landlord's consent first. We've asked them, including what should happen to the existing machine; we've noted that your new machine would stay yours and go with you when you leave. Please don't buy or disconnect anything until we confirm. You can't be asked to pay to remove or dispose of the landlord's machine. If you can, send a photo of the machine and any error code, as it helps us check it's really beyond repair. We'll update you by 29 July.

Request summary with context: The Willow Maintenance washing machine is experiencing a power failure and is not operational.

Tenant's original query: Washing machine broken, it’s LG , we have googled it, it has power failure and can’t be fixed, I am willing to replace, this one was here when I moved in, but if I replace it will be mine and not become part of the property, if I ever was to move out I would take it with me.

arguments.decision_needed: Tenant reports the landlord's LG washing machine (there when they moved in) has a power failure and they believe it can't be repaired (their own web research, not diagnosed). They offer to buy a replacement that would remain their property and be taken with them when they leave. Do you consent? And what should happen to the existing machine (inspect/repair, remove, dispose, store), and may the tenant's machine stay connected? Any disconnection, removal or fitting would be at your cost, not the tenant's.
options: Consent to tenant's own machine, landlord's machine removed/stored at landlord's cost (recommended if repair not worthwhile)
Send our contractor to inspect/repair the existing LG first
Landlord arranges own contractor or replacement
Decline tenant's own machine
arguments.update: No contractor assigned and no spend committed. Job is routine. Please reply by 2025-07-29.

arguments.note: Tenant wants to replace landlord's LG washer with own machine (remains tenant's, not on inventory, taken at move-out). Needs landlord consent; not a repair. Fault undiagnosed (tenant's online research). Landlord asked re existing machine disposal/storage at landlord cost and whether tenant's may stay connected. Awaiting landlord, review 2025-07-29.

arguments.body: Hello, thanks for letting us know about the washing machine. Because the machine belongs to the landlord, and you'd like to bring in your own, we need the landlord's consent first. We've asked them, including what should happen to the existing machine; we've noted that your new machine would stay yours and go with you when you leave. Please don't buy or disconnect anything until we confirm. You can't be asked to pay to remove or dispose of the landlord's machine. If you can, send a photo of the machine and any error code, as it helps us check it's really beyond repair. We'll update you by 29 July.

arguments.purpose: Chase landlord on consent to tenant's own washing machine and handling of existing LG; chase by second channel if none.
